title: Architecture Conformance Review
claim_boundary: This is a local architecture review of live source and executable contracts. It does not prove native behavior, hosted CI, release packaging, or public release readiness.

evidence.mechanism: Scans every production Dart file under lib/core and rejects imports or exports into lib/features.
Defines ownership of shared ProjectModel, AssetType, and command-history contracts in Core.

findings: The standing dependency-direction gate prevents Core from regressing into feature-owned layers.
Application composition remains allowed to know feature modules; this review does not treat router and shell orchestration as a Core dependency violation.

evidence.mechanism: Stores typed cross-workspace references instead of co-owning Character canon.
Pins read and write permission checks across workspace boundaries.
Pins affected-Novel review before Character deletion.
Pins separate filesystem namespaces and identifier validation.

findings: Novel and Character ownership remain distinct; links carry identity, role, visibility, and representation mode rather than a second canonical Character record.
Destructive Character lifecycle operations retain an explicit affected-Novel review boundary.

evidence.mechanism: Proves the highest-risk Core-to-feature edge is absent.
Documents logical Wave 1 dependency levels and workspace prerequisites.

findings: No Core-to-feature import is permitted by the executable gate.
There is no repository-wide directed import-graph cycle gate for feature-to-feature edges, so absence of all dependency cycles is not yet executable evidence.

evidence.mechanism: The live event payload exposes projectId, commandType, sequence, event type, and source.
Proves command events are published after mutation execution.
Defines the intended WS-EVENTS v1 names and no-canon-payload rule.

findings: The universal command bus is implemented and consumed, but the documented WS-EVENTS v1 names (ws.link.*, ws.projection.*, ws.character.*) are not represented by a typed production contract.
ProjectMutationEvent has no stable workspace event name or entity identifier, so consumers cannot implement the documented link/projection lifecycle contract without interpreting commandType strings.
This is a release-candidate architecture blocker to be resolved by a later implementation step; 112.4 records it and does not fabricate conformance.

evidence.mechanism: Pins the public plugin SDK contract.
Pins sandbox permission and isolation behavior.
Pins host lifecycle and boundary behavior.

findings: Plugin SDK, sandbox, repository, host, model, and UI boundaries have dedicated local test surfaces.
External third-party plugin compatibility remains outside this local conformance claim and belongs to Sprint 112.40.

evidence.mechanism: Pins transactional import rollback so failed cross-workspace materialization does not leave partial canonical data.
Pins rebuildable projection behavior rather than treating cache data as canonical truth.
Defines FISO-01 and the intended WorkspaceFailure taxonomy.

findings: Critical import atomicity, rebuildable projections, namespaces, and deletion review provide concrete failure containment.
The documented WorkspaceFailure validation/notFound/conflict/permissionDenied family is absent from production; service failures still use mixed exception types.
Failure isolation is therefore locally evidenced for selected workflows but not conformant as a uniform contract across all three waves.

blocking_findings: WS-EVENTS v1 is documented but not implemented as a typed workspace event contract.
Repository-wide feature import cycles are not covered by an executable graph gate.
FISO-01 typed WorkspaceFailure taxonomy is not uniformly implemented.
